title: Interim custody arrangements during a pending divorce
p1: A divorce can take months or even years to finish. But a child's daily life cannot stay uncertain until the final judgment arrives. So who decides where the child stays while the case is still going on?
p2: Many people assume that the parent who files for divorce automatically gets custody. That is not true. Courts can make temporary custody arrangements, often called interim custody, based on what serves the child's best interests during the pending case.
p3: Interim custody is not a final decision about who will raise the child forever. It is a practical arrangement that can decide living arrangements, visitation, schooling, and day-to-day care until the court examines the matter fully. A surprising point: even a parent who does not have physical custody may still play a meaningful role through regular visitation and involvement in the child's life. The focus is the child's stability, not winning a battle between parents.
conclusion: Do you think temporary custody decisions should prioritize the child's routine and emotional stability over the preferences of either parent?
